reuse.why: Reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and routes forecast, schedule actions, preview and the API model through getScheduledAmount; the budget template keeps its own op dispatch calling the worst-case helpers directly.

duplication.why: The approximate rule has a single definition (getApproxWorstCase) and the forecast's inline copy is removed, but the isbetween/isapprox/plain dispatch is now written both in getScheduledAmount and in schedule-template.ts.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getRangeWorstCase and getScheduledAmount, and the tolerance comes from shared/rules.ts where matching defines it.

scope.why: Only the amount rule, its call sites, tests and a release note change.

maintainability.why: Adding an optional op argument means any caller that omits it silently keeps the exact value: the desktop-client consumers (Balance, SchedulesTable, mobile schedules) still call getScheduledAmount without the op, and the template duplicates the dispatch.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList dispatches on op itself and calls getRangeWorstCase/getApproxWorstCase instead of getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The op-based dispatch of getScheduledAmount is reshaped as a nested ternary on amountCondition.op in schedule-template.ts.

one_place.where: The rule itself is getApproxWorstCase in shared/schedules.ts, but whether it applies depends on an optional op argument: the template re-implements the dispatch, and desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, MobileSchedulesPage.tsx, SchedulesListItem.tsx) pass no op and still get the exact value.
